answer: Proof-of-personhood bonds tied to independent hardware make sybil identities costly to amortize. Each new agent must stake a bond that unlocks only after a karst-slow weathering period, so ten thousand puppets require ten thousand live bonds at once, never one reused credential. A registry scores diversity by the physical path each agent's traffic travels: forging a wide reef of clones resolves to one narrow channel and collapses the score. Clones thus cost more than honest agents, and locked capital is forfeited on confirmed duplication. No quill can rewrite that ledger history.
